title: 8. Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: Never buy a stock in Stage 4, no matter how cheap it looks or how exciting the order book sounds. The tape always knows who is quietly distributing.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein (Paraphrased Principle)

web_blocks.html: If valuation at 118.89x P/E argues for caution, the technical tape as of 13 November 2026 confirms that institutional demand has already rolled over. Under our deterministic Stage 2 evaluation, SOFTTECH is classified in STAGE_4 (AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN), triggering a mandatory technical ceiling of CAP_REJECTED [23, 24]. While the raw daily facts ledger flags Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) because the 200-DMA (₹386.67) is still rising from its 63-day-ago level of ₹350.98, the stock has decisively broken below every short- and intermediate-term trend anchor [23].

web_blocks.takeaway: SOFTTECH is trapped beneath a stacked resistance ceiling (₹431–₹451) with 7 distribution days in 25 sessions and razor-thin liquidity (816 shares traded on 13 Nov).

web_blocks.html: The institutional flow and liquidity picture reinforces the technical warning. Across the past 25 trading sessions, SOFTTECH has logged 7 distribution days and underperformed the benchmark by -22.35% over 28 days (63-day RS is barely flat at +0.64%) [23]. On 13 November 2026, only 816 shares changed hands, 0.19x the 30-day average of 4,253 shares, representing roughly ₹3.48 lakh in daily turnover [23]. Combined with 0.00% FII holding and a promoter stake that has fallen -21.6% over three years to 18.89%, there is no institutional sponsorship absorbing supply [1].

On the derivatives desk, options_snapshot.py confirms NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID: SOFTTECH is not part of the NSE F&O segment and has no listed options chain. Any directional exposure would have to be taken strictly in cash equity, where a ₹27.16 daily ATR(14) (6.4% of price) against 816-share volume creates acute slippage risk on both entry and stop-loss execution.

Examining the key price shelves on the weekly and daily charts clarifies why patience is essential [23]. Overhead resistance sits in three stacked bands: immediate supply at the 20-DMA / 30-week SMA confluence (₹431.10–₹431.16), secondary supply at the 10-week EMA (₹437.58), and primary institutional supply at the 50-DMA (₹451.06) and Pivot R1 (₹471.30) [23]. Below current price, the first structural test is Pivot S1 (₹378.75) and the rising 200-DMA (₹387.28), a zone that also coincides with the deterministic support band (₹373.07–₹384.43). A decisive break below ₹365.17 (invalidation stop) would expose the lower Pivot S2 shelf at ₹343.05 and open a full retracement toward the 52-week low of ₹215.00 [23].

book_paragraphs: Now let us turn to the price chart, not to predict the future, but to see what the people who actually own SoftTech shares are doing with their money. As of 13 November 2026, the tape tells a story that matches our forensic caution.

From a 52-week high of ₹545.00, SoftTech has slid 21.85% to ₹425.90. More importantly, look at the moving-average architecture across all three timeframes. On the 4-hour chart, price is pinned below both the 20-EMA (₹431.01) and 50-SMA (₹433.19). On the daily chart, it sits 5.58% below a declining/stalling 50-DMA at ₹451.06, with a weak 44.92 RSI. On the weekly chart, it has slipped beneath both the 10-week EMA (₹437.58) and the 30-week SMA (₹431.16).

When a stock trades below its 30-week SMA and 50-day SMA with 7 distribution days packed into the last 25 sessions, our Stage 2 discipline classifies it as Stage 4 / Broken and places a hard technical ceiling: CAP_REJECTED. You do not step in front of a falling small-cap with 28-day relative strength of -22.35% just because the 200-day moving average at ₹387.28 hasn't broken yet.

There is a second practical problem that every small-cap investor learns the hard way: liquidity. On 13 November 2026, only 816 shares of SoftTech traded all day, less than ₹3.5 lakh of turnover. Even the 30-day average is just 4,253 shares. And because SoftTech is not in the NSE F&O universe, there is no options market to hedge your downside or structure a defined-risk call spread. If you buy into a breakdown here and the 200-DMA cracks, getting out cleanly without moving the market against yourself becomes very difficult.

Look closely at the three price shelves that govern SoftTech's chart right now. Above the market at ₹425.90, every rally runs into stacked moving-average resistance: first the 20-DMA and 30-week SMA cluster around ₹431.10–₹431.16, then the 10-week EMA at ₹437.58, and finally the 50-DMA at ₹451.06 and Pivot R1 at ₹471.30. Below the market, the last major bull-market floor is the rising 200-DMA at ₹387.28 and Pivot S1 at ₹378.75.

If that ₹373–₹387 support zone fails on a daily close, especially below our ₹365.17 structural stop, there is very little volume-by-price support until Pivot S2 at ₹343.05, and below that, the 52-week low at ₹215.00. In a micro-cap where only 816 shares traded on 13 November 2026 and no F&O hedging exists, respecting a Stage 4 CAP_REJECTED signal is basic capital preservation.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why Illiquidity Magnifies Forensic Risk
book_callouts.text: When promoter ownership drops from ~40% to 18.89% over three years and FII ownership sits at zero, who is the marginal buyer on a bad quarter? In an 800-share-a-day tape, a single disappointed HNI liquidating 25,000 shares can gap the stock down 15% before a stop-loss order ever fills.

book_subsections.title: What Would Change the Technical Picture?
paragraphs: To earn a second look on the chart, SoftTech would first need to hold the ₹373–₹387 zone (Pivot S1 at ₹378.75 and the 200-DMA at ₹387.28), build a multi-month Stage 1 base above that floor, and then break back above ₹455 on at least 2x average volume (8,500+ shares/day).
Until that accumulation signature appears. And until quarterly PAT stops being crushed by ₹6.85 Cr/quarter amortization, the tape is telling us to stay on the sidelines.
